findings.title: The process type check prevents hung workers from being killed
findings.body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker is classified as hung, its dictionary entry is replaced without killing it, leaving an untracked process that can resume flushing the same shards and updating the same health/backpressure values as its replacement. Check against SpawnProcess or BaseProcess and stop the old worker before replacing it.

findings.title: Continue worker cleanup after the join deadline expires
findings.body: If waiting for one flusher exhausts the timeout, this break skips termination of every remaining worker. It also skips all workers if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the deadline. Setting stopped only helps workers that return to the top of their loop; workers blocked in Redis or Kafka calls can remain alive after join returns and overlap with replacement flushers following a rebalance. The deadline should stop further waiting, but cleanup must still terminate every outstanding child.
